language: science
voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 }
app:
  command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8221
  url: http://127.0.0.1:8221/index.html
  readySelector: "#gpanel"
  layout: full
explainClip:
  query: { code: "@boards.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain }
  caption: "Stimulus to response"
  say: "A stimulus is any change the body detects, inside or outside it."
  clip:
    - caption: { text: "A stimulus is any change the body detects.", say: "A stimulus is any change the body detects." }
    - wait: 2290
    - click: "Touching a hot pan"
    - expect: { selector: "body", contains: "Arm muscles" }
    - caption: { text: "A change outside: receptors detect it, and muscles respond.", say: "A change outside: receptors detect it, and muscles respond." }

Earlier you met the body's systems, and now you'll see how your body notices a change and does something about it.

## Engage: what is a stimulus?

```step
stage: predict
insight: "Students who think stimuli are only things outside the body (light, sound, touch) will pick the narrow answer; the board includes changes inside."
check:
  type: predict
  q: "Which of these is a stimulus?"
  options: ["Only things outside you: light, sound, touch, heat", "Any change your body detects, outside or inside", "Only things that hurt", "Only things you notice"]
  actual: "Any change your body detects, outside or inside: blood sugar rising and body water falling are stimuli too, though you don't notice them."
```

## Explore: follow the signal

```step
stage: run
insight: "Watching five different stimuli travel through the same five boxes makes the pathway a pattern, not a list to memorise."
try: { playground: board, starter: "boards.yml#pathways", height: 540 }
check: { type: board, text: "Follow at least four stimuli through the pathway, including two internal ones.", when: "n >= 4" }
```

Click a stimulus to send it through the pathway. Notice which ones are **internal** and which are **external**.

## Explain: the pathway

```step
stage: investigate
insight: "Naming the part each step plays, and sorting internal from external, are the two pieces of the hinge."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: sort
      q: "Internal or external stimulus?"
      options: ["Internal", "External"]
      items:
        - ["A loud bang", "External"]
        - ["Blood sugar rising", "Internal"]
        - ["The smell of toast", "External"]
        - ["Body temperature falling", "Internal"]
        - ["Too little water in the blood", "Internal"]
        - ["Cold wind on your skin", "External", "The wind is outside; your body temperature falling because of it is an internal change."]
    hint: ["For each one, ask where the change is actually happening, out in the world or inside your body, and it still counts as a stimulus even if you'd never feel it.", "Go back to the board and click a few stimuli again, because the line under the pathway tells you whether each one is internal or external."]
  - check:
      type: match
      q: "Match each part of the pathway to what it does."
      pairs:
        - ["Stimulus", "A change inside or outside the body"]
        - ["Receptor", "Detects the change"]
        - ["Command centre", "Processes the information and decides"]
        - ["Effector", "A muscle or gland that carries out the response"]
        - ["Response", "What the body does"]
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "In the hot pan pathway, which is the effector?"
      options: ["The arm muscles", "The skin", "The spinal cord", "The heat"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "The skin is where the receptors are, so its job is noticing the heat, not moving your hand.", "The spinal cord is the command centre in this reflex.", "The heat is the stimulus."]
    hint: ["Think about what the skin is doing when you touch the pan, because noticing the heat and moving your hand are two different jobs.", "Click Touching a hot pan on the board again and read which box each of these options sits in."]
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "The smell of toast is the stimulus. Which is the receptor, and what does it do?"
      options: ["Smell receptors in the nose: they detect chemicals from the toast and send impulses to the brain", "The brain: it smells the toast", "The toast: it gives off the smell", "The salivary glands: they make your mouth water"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "The brain is the command centre: it makes sense of the impulses but can't detect chemicals in the air itself.", "The toast is where the stimulus comes from; receptors are part of your body.", "Glands that respond are effectors: they carry out the response."]
  - check: { type: reflect, text: "I can trace a stimulus through receptor, command centre and effector to a response, for one external and one internal change." }
```

## Elaborate: a new pathway

```step
stage: modify
tier: typical
insight: "Applying the pathway to an unseen example shows the pattern has transferred."
check:
  type: sort
  q: "A runner's muscles use oxygen fast, so carbon dioxide in the blood rises. Breathing speeds up. Sort each into its part of the pathway."
  options: ["Stimulus", "Receptor", "Command centre", "Effector", "Response"]
  items:
    - ["Carbon dioxide in the blood rises", "Stimulus"]
    - ["Chemical receptors in blood vessels and the brain", "Receptor"]
    - ["Brain stem", "Command centre"]
    - ["Diaphragm and rib muscles", "Effector"]
    - ["Faster, deeper breathing", "Response"]
hint: ["Go along the chain in the order it happens: what changed first, what notices it, what makes the call, and what actually does the breathing.", "Line it up with the hot pan, where the skin noticed, the spinal cord decided and the arm muscles acted, and find the item that plays each of those parts for breathing."]
```

## Elaborate: plants respond too

```step
stage: modify
tier: wider
insight: "Plants detect and respond to stimuli without nerves, which separates the pathway idea from the nervous system."
check:
  type: question
  q: "A seedling on a windowsill bends towards the light. Which part of the pathway is missing compared with your body?"
  options: ["There are no nerves: the command is a plant hormone (auxin) carried in the plant, not an impulse", "There is no stimulus", "There is no response", "Nothing is different"]
  answer: 0
  feedback: [null, "Light from one side is the stimulus.", "Bending is the response.", "Plants have no nervous system."]
  explain: "Plants still detect a stimulus and respond. They have no nerves, so bending towards light is coordinated by a hormone, auxin. (A few plants, like the Venus flytrap, also send fast electrical signals.)"
```

## Evaluate: look back

```step
stage: info
check: { type: reflect, text: "I compared my first answer about what a stimulus is with what I now know." }
```

Write one sentence: "At first I thought… Now I think… because…"

**Revision summary**

- A **stimulus** is any change the body detects, **external** (light, heat, sound) or **internal** (blood sugar, temperature, water).
- **Stimulus → receptor → command centre → effector → response.**
- Receptors detect; the brain, spinal cord or a gland decides; muscles and glands are the effectors.

```teacher
summary: Students identify stimuli as internal or external changes and trace
  them through the stimulus–response pathway (AC9S9U01, node 1, a hinge node).
time: 20
timing: Engage and Explore 7 min · Explain 8 min · Evaluate 3 min · Typical adds
  2 min, Wider about 2 min
goals:
  - I can explain that a stimulus is a change inside or outside the body.
  - I can name the parts of the stimulus–response pathway and what each does.
  - I can trace an internal and an external stimulus through the pathway.
before: >
  A concept tutorial for introducing or revising the idea; it does not replace a
  reaction-time practical (the ruler drop) or the knee-jerk reflex. Set the
  width with `?width=minimum`, `typical` (default) or `wider`.


  The hinge misconception is that stimuli are only external. Three of the five
  board stimuli are internal on purpose.


  Board notes: each pathway is simplified to one receptor, one command centre
  and one effector; in the blood sugar and water pathways the gland that
  releases the hormone sits with the command centre and the target organ (liver
  and muscle, kidneys) is the effector, as Signals and Nerve or hormone teach.
running:
  - "Engage: count how many chose 'only things outside you'."
  - "Explore: ask which stimuli they would never notice happening."
  - "Explain: the sort is the checkpoint; 'cold wind' prompts the external
    change / internal effect distinction."
struggle: Placing each part on the pathway, especially changes inside the body.
  When a student skips one, ask what detects the change and what carries out the
  response.
stuck:
  - see: A student says blood sugar isn't a stimulus because you can't feel it.
    ask: Did the body detect it and respond?
    fix: "Yes: cells in the pancreas detect it. A stimulus is anything the body
      detects, felt or not."
  - see: A student calls the skin the effector.
    ask: Does the skin detect the heat or move the hand?
    fix: "It detects it: receptors. Muscles and glands are effectors."
stretch: In the water pathway, the response makes the stimulus go away. Find
  another pathway on the board where that happens.
support: Give a five-box strip to fill in for each stimulus clicked.
leads: >
  Next: building pathways yourself and why the command centre matters (node 2),
  then nerves versus hormones (node 4) and feedback (node 5).


  In class: ruler-drop reaction times; knee-jerk reflex; pupil response with a
  torch.
exit:
  q: Give one internal stimulus and name its receptor and effector.
  a: "For example: body temperature rising; temperature receptors in the brain;
    sweat glands."
explain: >
  **Stimulus:** any change the body detects, inside or outside it. **Pathway:**
  stimulus → receptor (detects) → command centre (decides) → effector (muscle or
  gland) → response.
```
